claim: A Return to Targeted Adjudication On September 4, 2025, the day before withdrawing its appeals, the FTC filed a complaint against Gateway Pet Memorial Services, alleging that the company's widespread use of one-year non-competes in the pet cremation industry constituted an anticompetitive practice violating Section 5 of the FTC Act
evidence: The Federal Trade Commission filed a complaint against Gateway Services and its subsidiary Gateway US Holdings, Inc., (collectively referred to as Gateway), which alleges that Gateway imposed noncompete agreements on almost all of its employees, which typically prohibited employees from working in the pet cremation service industry anywhere in the U.S. for one year after leaving Gateway.
excerpt:
The Federal Trade Commission filed a complaint against Gateway Services and its subsidiary Gateway US Holdings, Inc., (collectively referred to as Gateway), which alleges that Gateway imposed noncompete agreements on almost all of its employees, which typically prohibited employees from working in the pet cremation service industry anywhere in the U.S. for one year after leaving Gateway.

On November 25, 2025, the FTC finalized the consent order in this matter.

PRESS RELEASE: FTC Approves Final Order Prohibiting Noncompete Enforcement by Gateway Services
